keySecurity.title: IP security of the access keys
keySecurity.intro: Who may reach /mcp, /api/v1 and the OAuth token endpoint of the connectors. A ban is a platform ban: it covers every web port of the edge — the panel, the client space, the webmail and every hosted site. A shared NAT address (office, 4G) that gets banned loses the sites too.
keySecurity.loadFailed: The access-key security settings could not be loaded
keySecurity.saveFailed: The settings could not be saved

modeHint.auto: Log only for 48 hours after the first start, then strict by itself (the platform admins are notified).
modeHint.log: Addresses outside every key are journaled ("would have banned"), never banned.
modeHint.on: When every active key has addresses, any other address that touches /mcp, /api/v1 or /oauth/token is banned without end.
modeHint.off: No intrusion ban. Repeated bad keys are still banned.

coverage.allowList: in the list of a key

status.title: Current state
status.autoAt: Strict from {{date}} (end of the 48 h log-only period).
status.ipNotCovered: Your current address ({{ip}}) is in no key's list: outside your panel session it would be banned in strict mode. Add it to the trusted IPs if you call the API from here.
status.openKeys: Open keys keeping the strict mode off ({{count}}):
status.whyTooWide: range too wide (wider than an IPv4 /16 or an IPv6 /48)

keySecurity.requireIp: An IP address is mandatory on the access keys
keySecurity.requireIpHint: Default of every workspace (a workspace may override it). A key without address is refused at use until restricted; a connector is covered by the connectors' ranges.
keySecurity.maxFailuresHint: From one address within the window, then a ban on the escalation ladder of the bans.
keySecurity.trustedIpsHint: Never banned by the key surfaces (their bad keys are refused, not counted). Your office, your CI runners.
keySecurity.connectorRangesHint: Where the Claude connectors call from (Anthropic's published outbound addresses). Always allowed for a connector and never banned. Empty: every connector counts as an open key.
keySecurity.cliHint: Locked out? From the server: docker exec <panel container> node dist/src/cli/keySecurity.js unban <ip> (or trust <ip>, status, help).

key.ipMissingHint: An IP address is mandatory on the keys of this workspace: this key is refused until you restrict it.
key.openHint: This open key (no allowed address) keeps the strict IP mode off for the whole platform.
key.connectorRangesHint: Added automatically: the outbound addresses of the connectors (Anthropic).
key.openBanner: Without an allowed address, this key can be used from anywhere, and an open key keeps the strict IP mode of the access keys off for the whole platform. An IP may also be mandatory in this workspace.
key.connectorBanner: Claude calls this connector from Anthropic's published outbound addresses: they are allowed automatically and never banned. Any other address must be listed here: a connector used from Claude Code or Claude Desktop calls from your own machine.

trust.title: Add to the trusted IPs
trust.confirm: Lift the platform ban of {{ip}} and add it to the trusted IPs of the access keys: it will never be banned by the key surfaces again.
trust.failed: The address could not be trusted

tenant.title: IP mandatory on the access keys
tenant.hint: A key without allowed address is refused in this workspace (connectors are covered by the connectors' ranges). Platform setting: Settings > API access & agents.
